chunks: Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:

I set out for an ʿUmrah and purchased a sacrificial camel while I was in al-Madīnah. So I sent to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and asked him how I should deal with it. He sent back to me: “What were you going to do with this? It would have sufficed you to buy one there from ʿArafah.”

And he said: “Go until you come to Masjid al-Shajarah, then face it toward the qiblah and make it kneel. Then enter the mosque and pray two rakʿahs. Then come out to it and mark it on the right side, then say: ‘In the Name of Allah. O Allah, from You and for You. O Allah, accept from me.’ Then when you ascend al-Baydāʾ, recite the talbiyah.”

key_terms.بَدَنَةً: a sacrificial camel offered in pilgrimage rites
key_terms.فَأَشْعِرْهَا: mark it as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ: the miqat mosque where the pilgrim begins the rite
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْدَاءَ: the place where the talbiyah is to be recited
key_terms.ٱلْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer toward which the animal is faced

ai.seo_question: How should a sacrificial camel be marked and prepared at Masjid al-Shajarah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the procedure for handling a sacrificial camel for ʿUmrah or hajj-related rites, including taking it to Masjid al-Shajarah, orienting it toward the qiblah, praying, marking it, and reciting a supplication. It also indicates that purchasing the animal later at ʿArafah would have been sufficient, reflecting practical legal guidance in pilgrimage rites.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2577 - Ibn Faddal narrated from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:
"I set out for Umrah and purchased a sacrificial camel while I was in Madinah. I sent a message to Abu Abdullah (as) asking him how I should handle it.
Imam (as) sent back a reply: 'What were you going to do with it? It would have sufficed for you to buy one in Arafat.'
Then Imam (as) said: 'Go to Masjid al-Shajarah, face it toward the Qiblah, and make it kneel. Then, enter the mosque and pray two units of prayer. After that, come out to the camel, mark it (Ish'ar) on its right side, and say:
In the name of Allah (swt). O Allah (swt), from You and for You. O Allah (swt), accept it from me.
When you ascend to al-Bayda', recite the Talbiyah.'"
